daily.next: add the model's fit-to-fit spread to the samples

gate.id: time_decision_gate_v4 (v1's, unchanged; the daily arm alone)
gate.chosen: the decision is chosen on every seed (an operating point; no refusal)
gate.time_split: every run's data stage split by time (the strategy recorded per run)
gate.capacity: on every seed that acted, the holdout's actions never exceed its capacity (a share of its rows with one row's rounding; or the day by day slots the record states), and the holdout was read once
gate.coverage: among the seeds that chose to act (at least 20), the realised value per customer lies inside the choice's 90% prediction interval on at least 80% of them
gate.centre: each seed's z = (realised - the interval's centre) / (its half-width / 1.645); |mean z| <= 1.645 / sqrt(N)
gate.width: the 90% chi-squared interval of the root mean square of z contains 1 (neither too narrow nor too wide)
gate.inconclusive: fewer than 20 seeds acting: no verdict on the interval
gate.next: a pass: keep the day by day interval, v3's coverage miss read as chance; too narrow (the width's interval above 1) with misses on both sides: add the model's fit-to-fit spread to the samples (the holdout is scored by the final model, the samples by one fold model never refitted; one call a day hangs on its fine ranking), and if the paired every-fold RMS z is above 1 too, the latest fold's smaller pool is not the cause; coverage below 80% with the width passing: pool v3's and v4's daily seeds (90) and read the pooled coverage and RMS z beside the gate; a centre off at the spread measured (|mean z| above 1.645 RMS z / sqrt(N); for routing only, the gate unchanged): above 0, if the folds' values rise from the first fold to the last, score the out-of-fold rows with models of the final size, otherwise read the seeds; below 0, correct the optimism of choosing the model; too wide: sample the latest two folds
gate.paired: each run also keeps the interval drawn from every fold (0.115.0's) on the same rows and seed, with its z: reported beside the gate, never gated
